label: fiction
title: The Undocumented Repair
setting: The court sits in the present-day fictional city of Aster Reach. Shortly after one o’clock in the morning, an alarm drew patrol officer Dax Mere into the municipal evidence archive. He met an unidentified person inside and died before help arrived. Lena Voss, the technician responsible for the archive alarm, now stands accused of murdering an on-duty police officer.
charge: murder of an on-duty police officer
elements: The accused caused the on-duty officer’s death.
The accused intended to kill or cause really serious injury.
The killing was not legally justified or excused.
hook: Lena Voss hid an overnight archive visit and first told investigators she stayed home. Officer Dax Mere died answering an alarm shortly after one. The jury must decide whether her lie covered a rushed repair—or whether she was still inside when he arrived.

accused.human: Lena Voss, 38, has maintained municipal alarm systems for eleven years. Her work involves overnight callouts, shared maintenance credentials, and confidential access cards. Weeks before Dax’s death, a supervisor warned her for failing to document repairs. She says professional embarrassment explains her hidden visit and first false account, but not the killing.
accused.if_guilty: If convicted, sentencing would be decided separately by the judge. The jury’s task is limited to deciding whether the prosecution proved the charge.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Dax Mere answered an alarm as part of his ordinary duty and was deliberately killed inside the archive. Lena had secretly entered with her service card, concealed an unauthorised repair, and first told investigators she stayed home. Dax had noted he planned to ask her about that unexplained access. You will also hear from the officer who followed him and from the transit supervisor who says she saw Lena leave. The prosecution says weigh her deception with the whole night before deciding whether it surrounded a repair or a murder.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: Lena’s lie made her a proper suspect, and the defence will not excuse it. But a hidden repair is not proof of homicide. Sela Rune checked Lena’s photo pass at East Quay, spoke to her by name, and watched her board the waiting carriage. A signed repair note places Lena’s unfinished work before that journey, not during Dax’s call. Dax’s radio proves he met someone inside; it does not identify who. The defence says those independent accounts place Lena away before he entered the archive.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Lena’s concealed entry, false account, and knowledge that an alarm could bring a patrol officer are not trivial. A pass can be carried by someone else, and a supervisor can be mistaken about a face on a busy platform. Yet you must also confront the signed repair note and Sela’s direct recognition. The prosecution bears the burden on identity as well as the agreed homicide and intent. If those accounts leave you unsure Lena met Dax, suspicion—even serious suspicion—cannot lawfully complete the case.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The chronology is now complete. Lena finished a dishonest repair, left a signed note, walked to East Quay, and was recognised by name before she boarded. She remained aboard through the fatal window while Dax answered the alarm. Her lie concerned shame about an unauthorised work ticket, and it properly damaged her credibility with this jury. It did not identify the person on Dax’s radio, invent a face for that encounter, or prove she caused his death beyond reasonable doubt.

epilogue: After the proceedings, the city required written tickets for every overnight archive repair. Dax Mere’s sister kept pressing for answers about who met him inside. Lena Voss left overnight alarm work while the employment inquiry examined her hidden repair. The two families continued living with different parts of the same unresolved night.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: How well did you know Dax Mere?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: We partnered for eighteen months. He was careful and kind, checked my reports without making me feel small, and called his sister after every night shift.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What did an archive alarm usually require?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: The first officer checked the entrance, announced their presence, and waited if anything looked wrong. Dax didn’t treat routine calls casually.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What happened on his final call?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: Dispatch sent him at 1:16. His radio connected at 1:18. I heard him ask someone to stop, then the sound broke up. I followed when he didn’t answer.

beats.text: How well did you know Dax Mere? We partnered for eighteen months. He was careful and kind, checked my reports without making me feel small, and called his sister after every night shift. What did an archive alarm usually require? The first officer checked the entrance, announced their presence, and waited if anything looked wrong. Dax didn’t treat routine calls casually. What happened on his final call? Dispatch sent him at 1:16. His radio connected at 1:18. I heard him ask someone to stop, then the sound broke up. I followed when he didn’t answer.
beats.reveal_note: Eren’s first-hand account established when Dax began the call and treated him as a person, but it did not identify who attacked him.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: The parties agree that a qualified forensic physician examined Dax and reviewed the emergency records. Dax died between 1:19 and 1:24 from deliberate force by another person. Those findings exclude accident, natural illness, and self-infliction. They also prove the attacker intended to kill or cause really serious injury and acted without lawful justification. In legal terms, causation, murderous intent, and absence of justification are agreed. The prosecution must still prove the remaining element: that Lena was the attacker.
beats.reveal_note: The agreed medical evidence proved an unlawful intentional homicide within a defined window. It was deliberately neutral about who committed it.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: Investigators recovered Lena’s signed repair notebook from the plant room. The last entry, in her handwriting, records a completed sensor reset at 1:05 and initials her name. A lobby attendant later said he thought he glimpsed her coat near half past one, but admitted he never spoke to her and never checked a watch. The notebook proves she claimed to finish work at 1:05. The attendant’s glance proves nothing about identity or exact time.
beats.reveal_note: The notebook supported Lena’s repair story while the attendant’s vague glance invited over-reading. Neither placed her with Dax during the fatal window.

beats.speaker: w1

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: You never saw the person Dax met?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. I was still outside. I only heard his radio.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: And you cannot identify the voice as Lena’s?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: I can’t. It’s brief and distorted.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Dax never says Lena’s name or describes the person?

turns.speaker: w1
turns.text: No. The radio proves he met someone inside during the fatal window. It doesn’t tell me who that person was, and I won’t pretend it does.

beats.text: You never saw the person Dax met? No. I was still outside. I only heard his radio. And you cannot identify the voice as Lena’s? I can’t. It’s brief and distorted. Dax never says Lena’s name or describes the person? No. The radio proves he met someone inside during the fatal window. It doesn’t tell me who that person was, and I won’t pretend it does.
beats.reveal_note: Eren resisted overstating the fatal radio. It established an encounter but supplied no usable identification.

beats.speaker: pc
beats.text: The archive desk produced the signed overnight access register. Lena’s service card opened the archive at 12:47. No later entry used it, although lobby exits needed no card. Lena omitted the visit and first said she stayed home. Dax’s signed call note says he planned to ask her about the unexplained access. The register proves use of her card at 12:47, not how long she remained or who carried it.
beats.reveal_note: The access register and Lena’s lie established a concealed visit. They did not extend that visit into the medical window.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What is your job, and where were you that night?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: I supervise the East Quay night gate. At 1:16 I checked photo passes myself because the automatic reader had jammed twice that hour.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did you recognise Lena Voss?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Yes. Her pass photo matched her face. I said good evening by name; she answered and looked tired. She boarded the 1:18 westbound carriage while I watched the platform.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Could she have left and returned during the next ten minutes?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. I rode the same carriage to West Crossing for a shift handover. She stayed in the second bay until we arrived at 1:29. The nearest return walk to the archive takes about ten minutes.

beats.text: What is your job, and where were you that night? I supervise the East Quay night gate. At 1:16 I checked photo passes myself because the automatic reader had jammed twice that hour. Did you recognise Lena Voss? Yes. Her pass photo matched her face. I said good evening by name; she answered and looked tired. She boarded the 1:18 westbound carriage while I watched the platform. Could she have left and returned during the next ten minutes? No. I rode the same carriage to West Crossing for a shift handover. She stayed in the second bay until we arrived at 1:29. The nearest return walk to the archive takes about ten minutes.
beats.reveal_note: Sela’s direct recognition, conversation, and continuous observation placed Lena away during the fatal window.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What else did you recover about Lena’s repair?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: After the arrest I was shown her notebook because my gate log named her. The 1:05 entry is in the same hand as her signed staff card application, which the parties accept.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Does that notebook prove she left when she says?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: It proves she wrote that she finished at 1:05. My meeting with her at the gate at 1:16 is what proves she had already left the archive.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did anyone suggest you were mistaken about her face?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Investigators asked. I had spoken to her twice that month about jammed readers. I am sure of the person I greeted.

beats.text: What else did you recover about Lena’s repair? After the arrest I was shown her notebook because my gate log named her. The 1:05 entry is in the same hand as her signed staff card application, which the parties accept. Does that notebook prove she left when she says? It proves she wrote that she finished at 1:05. My meeting with her at the gate at 1:16 is what proves she had already left the archive. Did anyone suggest you were mistaken about her face? Investigators asked. I had spoken to her twice that month about jammed readers. I am sure of the person I greeted.
beats.reveal_note: The notebook supported timing; Sela’s prior acquaintance made her recognition more than a glance at a stranger.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: A photo pass can be carried by someone who resembles the holder?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: In theory. I compared the face in front of me with the photo and spoke her name. She answered.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: The carriage was busy. Could you have lost sight of her?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Not for long. I stood in the same bay. She did not leave her seat before West Crossing.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: So your evidence cannot explain why she lied about staying home?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. I can only say where she was from 1:16 to 1:29. I cannot explain her earlier choices.

Could you have lost sight of her? Not for long. I stood in the same bay. She did not leave her seat before West Crossing. So your evidence cannot explain why she lied about staying home? No. I can only say where she was from 1:16 to 1:29. I cannot explain her earlier choices.
beats.reveal_note: The prosecution tested recognition and left Lena’s lie unexplained, without breaking the alibi window.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What mistake had you made at the archive?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I’d rushed an alarm repair and never opened the required work ticket. After my earlier warning, I panicked about losing trusted callout work.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Why did you return that night?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I thought I could finish the repair and document it the next morning. That was dishonest and stupid, but I didn’t expect Dax or anyone else.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What do you remember about leaving?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I signed the notebook, locked my tools, walked quickly to East Quay, used my pass, and spoke briefly with Sela at the gate. I stayed aboard to West Crossing.

beats.text: What mistake had you made at the archive? I’d rushed an alarm repair and never opened the required work ticket. After my earlier warning, I panicked about losing trusted callout work. Why did you return that night? I thought I could finish the repair and document it the next morning. That was dishonest and stupid, but I didn’t expect Dax or anyone else. What do you remember about leaving? I signed the notebook, locked my tools, walked quickly to East Quay, used my pass, and spoke briefly with Sela at the gate. I stayed aboard to West Crossing.
beats.reveal_note: Lena gave a human explanation rather than reciting the records. Her account still required independent support, which the jury had already heard.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: You first told investigators you had stayed home?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Yes. I lied because I was ashamed and afraid of another warning. I corrected it when they showed me the access record.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: You knew how to silence an archive alarm?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: For maintenance, yes, like three other technicians on the same roster.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: And you knew an alarm could bring a patrol officer?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Of course. I believed the repair had cleared it. I didn’t attack Dax, and I was already on the carriage when he arrived.

beats.text: You first told investigators you had stayed home? Yes. I lied because I was ashamed and afraid of another warning. I corrected it when they showed me the access record. You knew how to silence an archive alarm? For maintenance, yes, like three other technicians on the same roster. And you knew an alarm could bring a patrol officer? Of course. I believed the repair had cleared it. I didn’t attack Dax, and I was already on the carriage when he arrived.
beats.reveal_note: The cross-examination secured Lena’s lie and technical access while leaving the independent alibi intact.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: For orientation, the parties agree these times. Lena’s card entered the archive at 12:47. Her notebook records a finished repair at 1:05. Sela Rune checked her pass at East Quay at 1:16 and watched her board at 1:18. They remained on the same carriage until West Crossing at 1:29. Dax’s radio connected at 1:18; the fatal encounter occurred between 1:19 and 1:24. The sequence does not explain Lena’s lie or identify the person he met.
beats.reveal_note: The agreed chronology lets first-time jurors compare every event without mixing guesses about cameras or clocks.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: The charge has three elements. First, the prosecution must prove Lena caused Dax’s death. Because everyone agrees another person deliberately killed him, that element turns on identity: was Lena that person? Second, the attacker must have intended to kill or cause really serious injury. Third, the killing must lack lawful justification or excuse. Intent and absence of justification are agreed, but that agreement cannot prove identity. The prosecution bears the burden throughout. Lena does not have to identify the attacker, prove her journey, or explain every lie. A false account may damage credibility or support an inference, but it cannot replace proof of an element. Circumstantial evidence may be sufficient; assess what each record proves and what it cannot prove. If, after considering all the evidence, you are not sure the prosecution proved every element beyond reasonable doubt, your verdict must be Not Guilty. Use only evidence heard in court and do not research the case.
beats.reveal_note: The direction separates the agreed homicide from disputed identity and states the criminal standard without converting any imaginable doubt into reasonable doubt.

twist: The authors’ reference resolution is Not Guilty. Sela’s recognition and continuous observation place Lena on the carriage during the fatal window, and the signed repair note explains her earlier presence without proving she stayed. The strongest prosecution interpretation is that her hidden visit, lie, and alarm knowledge show planned deception. Those facts are probative, but they do not overcome the alibi or identify her as the person Dax met.

jurors.label: Juror 2 — Anya
jurors.persona: Starts with the vivid lobby image, then asks whether its timestamp deserves the same confidence.

agree: She hid the visit and lied. That still feels like guilt to me.
pushback: Wait—does a lie about a repair prove she was upstairs at 1:20?
concede: All right, Sela spoke to her by name on the platform. That changes the timeline.
burden_drift: She lied first. Why shouldn’t she have to fill every missing minute?
burden_correct: No, that’s backwards. Her lie is evidence, but the prosecution still has to identify Dax’s attacker.
final: I’m not sure Lena was there for the fatal encounter.

jurors.label: Juror 3 — Bram
jurors.persona: Keeps separating an authenticated file from the inference someone wants drawn from it.

agree: The access register proves the secret visit. I don’t think we can minimise that.
pushback: But 12:47 isn’t 1:20. What bridges that gap?
concede: The supervisor’s recognition and the notebook give a measured path out, not a guess.
burden_drift: I keep wanting a complete account from Lena because the work ticket is missing.
burden_correct: The evidence still has to satisfy the prosecution’s burden; suspicion can’t complete it.
final: The reliable times don’t place Lena with Dax.

jurors.label: Juror 4 — Cora
jurors.persona: Keeps returning the room to disputed identity when strong feelings pull it toward the agreed homicide.

agree: The defence timeline is supported by records created before anyone was accused.
pushback: Who can identify Lena in Dax’s final recording? Nobody has.
concede: I accept the lie was serious. I don’t accept that it identifies a murderer.
burden_drift: The concealment is tempting us to demand that Lena prove innocence.
burden_correct: The judge told us what to ask: are we sure the prosecution proved every element?
final: I’m holding out because identity hasn’t been proved.

jurors.label: Juror 5 — Dev
jurors.persona: Initially trusts the simple lobby-glance story, but changes position when recognition and carriage records are tested.

agree: The secret visit is genuine. That’s why I started on Guilty.
pushback: A hidden repair is real. Why are we treating that as proof she met Dax?
concede: Sela’s recognition and the carriage ride put Lena away during the fatal window.
burden_drift: Part of me still wants Lena to solve this because she caused the repair mess.
burden_correct: A hidden repair isn’t a killing. We can’t blur them together.
final: I changed my mind once the repair note and transit observation lined up.

jurors.label: Juror 6 — Pax
jurors.persona: Organises the discussion by proposition and stops the room from treating agreed homicide as agreed identity.

agree: Let’s mark it clearly: Lena entered, hid the visit, and lied.
pushback: Now the next question: what proves she stayed for Dax’s arrival?
concede: Once the notebook and Sela’s recognition line up, the records fit together.
burden_drift: We’re starting to make Lena’s lie carry a duty to prove innocence.
burden_correct: Identity is still the prosecution’s element. Has it been proved beyond reasonable doubt?
final: The homicide is agreed. Lena’s identity as the attacker isn’t.

jurors.label: Juror 7 — Fia
jurors.persona: Speaks before settling, then corrects herself aloud when another juror exposes a missing step.

agree: I’ll be honest: the secret visit plus the lie looked decisive to me.
pushback: Hold on. A hidden repair can be true without placing her in the archive at 1:20.
concede: Yes, I see it now—Sela’s named recognition makes the alibi concrete.
burden_drift: Because Lena hid the repair, I keep wanting her to remove every doubt.
burden_correct: That isn’t her job. The prosecution has to prove the identity element.
final: I was anchored by the first image, and I’ve changed my view.

jurors.label: Juror 8 — Garen
jurors.persona: Tests whether independent evidence confirms the same proposition and is willing to reverse an early position.

agree: The secret visit first made me treat Lena as the obvious attacker.
pushback: But what places her inside during the radio call? Not the attendant’s vague glance.
concede: The independent sources show my first reading was wrong.
burden_drift: Lena’s dishonesty makes an unsupported inference feel safer than it is.
burden_correct: The prosecution must prove the fatal encounter, not merely an earlier visit.
final: The verified sequence puts Lena away before Dax met the attacker.

jurors.label: Juror 9 — Hale
jurors.persona: Listens for the limit in each witness’s answer and challenges anyone who quietly goes beyond it.

agree: Eren was careful: Dax met someone, but the recording identifies nobody.
pushback: Are we joining an earlier clear face to a later shadow and calling them one person?
concede: Lena’s lie damages her. The transit records still support why she said she left.
burden_drift: Dax’s death is terrible, and that can make unexplained conduct feel like guilt.
burden_correct: The seriousness of the charge makes accurate identification more important, not less.
final: I can’t identify Lena as Dax’s attacker.

jurors.label: Juror 10 — Iri
jurors.persona: Reacts strongly to Lena’s lie and has to be challenged when suspicion starts shifting the burden.

agree: Dax planned to question Lena. That gives the lie a sharper edge.
pushback: Still, a workplace cover-up doesn’t identify a murderer.
concede: I can’t brush aside a face on a centrally timed carriage.
burden_drift: Lena lied first, so I want her to tell us who else was inside.
burden_correct: No—that puts it on her. The prosecution has to prove Lena was the attacker.
final: I dislike what she did, but I’m not sure she committed murder.

jurors.label: Juror 11 — Joss
jurors.persona: Voices uncertainty as the sequence develops and corrects his own shorthand when it stops fitting.

agree: I followed the simple story: she hid the visit, so she must have stayed.
pushback: But that story skips the platform check. What happens when Sela places her on the carriage?
concede: The repair note, gate, and carriage now make one sequence for me.
burden_drift: I keep thinking Lena should fill the gap because she was dishonest.
burden_correct: Actually, the gap belongs to the prosecution’s case, doesn’t it?
final: The reliable sequence leaves Lena away from the fatal encounter.

jurors.label: Juror 12 — Kemi
jurors.persona: Insists on stating the strongest argument for each side before deciding what remains unproved.

agree: The signed repair note and Sela’s transit observation support one another without inventing a shared clock.
pushback: The prosecution’s best point is concealment. Which record carries it into the fatal window?
concede: I agree Lena’s denial made her a proper suspect and deserved investigation.
burden_drift: It’s easy to ask Lena for the answer because Dax’s attacker remains unknown.
burden_correct: An unknown attacker doesn’t reduce the prosecution’s burden.
final: The evidence proves a hidden visit, not the charged murder.
